name: Temporalis
origin: Temporal fossa of skull
insertion: Coronoid process and anterior ramus of mandible
notes: Muscle of mastication; palpate at the temple while clenching.

name: Masseter
origin: Zygomatic arch (and zygomatic process of maxilla)
insertion: Angle and lateral ramus of mandible
notes: Strongest jaw closer; palpate at the angle of the jaw while clenching.

name: Medial pterygoid
origin: Medial surface of lateral pterygoid plate (sphenoid)
insertion: Medial surface of ramus and angle of mandible
notes: Forms a sling with the masseter around the angle of the mandible.

name: Lateral pterygoid
origin: Greater wing and lateral surface of lateral pterygoid plate (sphenoid)
insertion: Neck of mandibular condyle, TMJ disk and capsule
notes: Only muscle of mastication that opens the mouth; pulls the disk forward.

name: Suprahyoids (digastric, mylohyoid, geniohyoid, stylohyoid)
origin: Mandible, mastoid notch and styloid process of temporal bone
insertion: Hyoid bone
nerve: Trigeminal (CN V), facial (CN VII), C1 via hypoglossal
notes: Raise the hyoid for swallowing; assist opening the mouth.

name: Infrahyoids (sternohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid, omohyoid)
origin: Sternum, thyroid cartilage, superior border of scapula (omohyoid)
insertion: Hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage
notes: Stabilize the hyoid so suprahyoids can open the mouth; aid swallowing and speech.

name: Sternocleidomastoid
origin: Sternal head: manubrium; clavicular head: medial 1/3 of clavicle
insertion: Mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line
stretch: Neck extension, lateral flexion to opposite side, rotation to same side
notes: Turning the head left uses the right SCM. Tight in torticollis.

name: Scalene, anterior
origin: Transverse processes C3-C6 (anterior tubercles)
insertion: 1st rib (scalene tubercle)
stretch: Neck lateral flexion to opposite side with extension (shoulder depressed)
notes: Brachial plexus passes between anterior and middle scalenes (thoracic outlet syndrome).

name: Scalene, middle
origin: Transverse processes C2-C7 (posterior tubercles)
insertion: 1st rib (behind subclavian groove)
stretch: Neck lateral flexion to opposite side with extension (shoulder depressed)
notes: Brachial plexus passes between anterior and middle scalenes (thoracic outlet syndrome).

name: Scalene, posterior
origin: Transverse processes C4-C6 (posterior tubercles)
insertion: 2nd rib
stretch: Neck lateral flexion to opposite side with extension (shoulder depressed)
notes: Accessory muscle of inspiration.

name: Prevertebrals (longus colli, longus capitis, rectus capitis anterior & lateralis)
origin: Anterior bodies and transverse processes of cervical and upper thoracic vertebrae
insertion: Occiput (basilar part) and upper cervical vertebrae
notes: Deep neck flexors (chin tuck); weak after whiplash.

name: Splenius capitis
origin: Lower ligamentum nuchae, spinous processes C7-T3
insertion: Mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line
stretch: Head/neck flexion, rotation and lateral flexion to opposite side

name: Splenius cervicis
origin: Spinous processes T3-T6
insertion: Transverse processes C1-C3 (posterior tubercles)
stretch: Neck flexion, rotation and lateral flexion to opposite side

name: Suboccipitals (rectus capitis posterior major & minor, obliquus capitis superior & inferior)
origin: Spinous process of C2, posterior tubercle and transverse process of C1
insertion: Occiput (inferior nuchal line) and transverse process of C1
notes: Fine postural control of the head; tight with forward-head posture.

name: Rectus abdominis
origin: Pubic crest and pubic symphysis
insertion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages 5-7
notes: Segmented 'six-pack' muscle; the linea alba separates right and left sides.

name: External oblique
origin: External surfaces of lower 8 ribs (5-12)
insertion: Anterior iliac crest, linea alba, pubic tubercle (via aponeurosis)
stretch: Trunk extension, lateral flexion to opposite side, rotation to same side
notes: Fibers run 'hands in pockets'; pairs with the opposite internal oblique for rotation.

name: Internal oblique
origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, anterior iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament
insertion: Inferior borders of ribs 10-12, linea alba, pubis (conjoint tendon)
stretch: Trunk extension, lateral flexion and rotation to opposite side
notes: Fibers run perpendicular to the external oblique.

name: Transverse abdominis
origin: Internal surfaces of costal cartilages 7-12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament
insertion: Linea alba and pubic crest (conjoint tendon)
stretch: No joint motion; relaxes with full inspiration
notes: Deepest abdominal; acts like a corset for core stability. Produces no trunk motion.

name: Iliocostalis (erector spinae)
origin: Sacrum, iliac crest, angles of ribs (common erector spinae tendon)
insertion: Angles of ribs and cervical transverse processes
stretch: Trunk and neck flexion, lateral flexion to opposite side
notes: Most lateral column of the erector spinae. Erector spinae (I Love Spaghetti: lateral to medial) are the prime trunk extensors.

name: Longissimus (erector spinae)
origin: Sacrum, iliac crest, transverse processes of lumbar-thoracic vertebrae
insertion: Transverse processes above, lower ribs, mastoid process
stretch: Trunk and neck flexion, lateral flexion to opposite side
notes: Middle and largest column of the erector spinae. Erector spinae (I Love Spaghetti: lateral to medial) are the prime trunk extensors.

name: Spinalis (erector spinae)
origin: Spinous processes of upper lumbar and lower thoracic vertebrae (and C7)
insertion: Spinous processes of upper thoracic and cervical vertebrae
stretch: Trunk and neck flexion, lateral flexion to opposite side
notes: Most medial column of the erector spinae. Erector spinae (I Love Spaghetti: lateral to medial) are the prime trunk extensors.

name: Semispinalis (transversospinalis)
origin: Transverse processes C4-T12
insertion: Spinous processes C2-T4 and occiput (between nuchal lines)
actions: Head, neck and upper trunk extension (bilateral)
stretch: Trunk/neck flexion and rotation to same side
notes: Semispinalis capitis is a major head extensor.

name: Multifidus (transversospinalis)
origin: Sacrum, PSIS, lumbar mammillary processes, thoracic transverse processes, cervical articular processes
insertion: Spinous processes 2-4 segments above
stretch: Trunk/neck flexion and rotation to same side
notes: Thickest in the lumbar region; key segmental stabilizer.

name: Rotatores (transversospinalis)
origin: Transverse processes
insertion: Lamina/spinous process 1-2 segments above
stretch: Trunk/neck flexion and rotation to same side
notes: Best developed in the thoracic region; important for proprioception.

name: Interspinales
origin: Spinous process of vertebra below
insertion: Spinous process of adjacent vertebra above
notes: Short segmental muscles, best developed in cervical and lumbar regions.

name: Intertransversarii
origin: Transverse process of vertebra below
insertion: Transverse process of adjacent vertebra above
actions: Trunk and neck lateral flexion (same side, assist)
nerve: Posterior & anterior rami of spinal nerves
notes: Short segmental stabilizers.

name: Quadratus lumborum
origin: Posterior iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament
insertion: 12th rib and transverse processes L1-L4
stretch: Trunk lateral flexion to opposite side (pelvis lowered on same side)
notes: Hikes the hip to clear the foot (e.g., stiff knee or long leg brace).

name: Diaphragm
origin: Xiphoid, inner surfaces of lower 6 ribs/costal cartilages, L1-L3 vertebral bodies (crura)
insertion: Central tendon
notes: 'C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive' - SCI at or above C3 needs ventilator support.

name: External intercostals
origin: Inferior border of rib above
insertion: Superior border of rib below (fibers run down and forward)
notes: Work with the diaphragm in quiet inspiration.

name: Internal intercostals
origin: Superior border of rib below
insertion: Inferior border of rib above (fibers run down and back)
notes: Fibers at right angles to external intercostals; parasternal fibers may assist inspiration.

name: Levatores costarum
origin: Transverse processes C7-T11
insertion: Rib below, between tubercle and angle
notes: Accessory muscle of deep inspiration.

name: Serratus posterior superior
origin: Ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes C7-T3
insertion: Superior borders of ribs 2-5
notes: Accessory muscle of deep inspiration.

name: Serratus posterior inferior
origin: Spinous processes T11-L2 (thoracolumbar fascia)
insertion: Inferior borders of ribs 9-12
notes: Accessory muscle of forced expiration.

name: Trapezius, upper
origin: External occipital protuberance, medial superior nuchal line, ligamentum nuchae
insertion: Lateral 1/3 of clavicle and acromion
stretch: Scapular depression and downward rotation, with neck lateral flexion to opposite side
notes: Force couple with lower trapezius and serratus anterior for upward rotation. Reverse action helps lift the trunk in crutch walking. CN XI injury causes shoulder drop/weak shrug.

name: Trapezius, middle
origin: Spinous processes C7-T3
insertion: Acromion and superior lip of spine of scapula
notes: Weak with rounded-shoulder posture.

name: Trapezius, lower
origin: Spinous processes T4-T12
insertion: Root (medial end) of spine of scapula

name: Levator scapulae
origin: Transverse processes C1-C4
insertion: Medial border of scapula, superior angle to root of spine
stretch: Scapular depression and upward rotation, neck flexion and lateral flexion/rotation to opposite side
notes: Common site of neck tension; forced inspiration in reverse action.

name: Rhomboid major
origin: Spinous processes T2-T5
insertion: Medial border of scapula, root of spine to inferior angle
notes: Works with rhomboid minor; antagonist to serratus anterior.

name: Rhomboid minor
origin: Ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes C7-T1
insertion: Medial border of scapula at root of spine

name: Serratus anterior
origin: External surfaces of upper 8-9 ribs
insertion: Anterior (costal) surface of medial border of scapula
notes: Holds scapula to the thorax; long thoracic nerve injury causes scapular winging. Needed for full arm flexion.

name: Pectoralis minor
origin: Ribs 3-5 (anterior)
insertion: Coracoid process of scapula
stretch: Scapular retraction, elevation, upward rotation (doorway/corner stretch)
notes: Only shoulder girdle muscle on the anterior body. Tightness contributes to rounded shoulders and thoracic outlet syndrome.

name: Deltoid, anterior
origin: Lateral 1/3 of clavicle
insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of humerus
stretch: Shoulder extension/hyperextension, horizontal abduction, external rotation
notes: Humeral positioner.

name: Deltoid, middle
origin: Acromion process
insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of humerus
stretch: Shoulder adduction (arm across body or behind back)
notes: Force couple with the rotator cuff during abduction. Axillary nerve injury (e.g., shoulder dislocation) weakens abduction.

name: Deltoid, posterior
origin: Spine of scapula
insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of humerus
stretch: Shoulder flexion, horizontal adduction, internal rotation

name: Pectoralis major, clavicular head
origin: Medial half of clavicle
insertion: Lateral lip of bicipital (intertubercular) groove
stretch: Shoulder extension, horizontal abduction, external rotation
notes: Whole muscle: adduction, horizontal adduction, internal rotation. Humeral propeller.

name: Pectoralis major, sternal head
origin: Sternum, costal cartilages 1-6, aponeurosis of external oblique
insertion: Lateral lip of bicipital (intertubercular) groove
actions: Shoulder extension (from flexion, about 180 to 120 degrees)
stretch: Shoulder flexion/abduction overhead, horizontal abduction, external rotation
notes: Whole muscle: adduction, horizontal adduction, internal rotation. Used for depression transfers/push-ups.

name: Supraspinatus
origin: Supraspinous fossa of scapula
insertion: Greater tubercle of humerus (superior facet)
notes: Rotator cuff (SITS). Most commonly torn/impinged cuff tendon.

name: Infraspinatus
origin: Infraspinous fossa of scapula
insertion: Greater tubercle of humerus (middle facet)
notes: Rotator cuff (SITS); depresses and stabilizes the humeral head.

name: Teres minor
origin: Upper 2/3 of lateral (axillary) border of scapula
insertion: Greater tubercle of humerus (inferior facet)
notes: Rotator cuff (SITS).

name: Subscapularis
origin: Subscapular fossa of scapula
insertion: Lesser tubercle of humerus
notes: Rotator cuff (SITS); only cuff muscle on the anterior scapula and on the lesser tubercle.

name: Latissimus dorsi
origin: Spinous processes T7-L5, thoracolumbar fascia, posterior iliac crest, lower 3-4 ribs
insertion: Floor of bicipital (intertubercular) groove
stretch: Shoulder flexion, abduction, external rotation (with trunk lateral flexion to opposite side)
notes: Humeral propeller; key for depression transfers, wheelchair push-ups and crutch walking.

name: Teres major
origin: Inferior angle and lower lateral border of scapula
insertion: Medial lip of bicipital groove (crest of lesser tubercle)
notes: 'Lat's little helper'; not part of the rotator cuff.

name: Coracobrachialis
origin: Coracoid process of scapula
insertion: Middle of medial humeral shaft

name: Biceps brachii
origin: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle; short head: coracoid process
insertion: Radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis
stretch: Shoulder extension + elbow extension + forearm pronation
notes: Strongest elbow flexor with forearm supinated. Also covered in u3-s2 and u4-s7.

name: Brachialis
origin: Distal half of anterior humerus
insertion: Coronoid process and ulnar tuberosity
notes: 'Workhorse' elbow flexor: flexes in any forearm position because it inserts on the ulna.

name: Brachioradialis
origin: Proximal 2/3 of lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus
insertion: Radial styloid process
notes: Strongest in midposition (hammer curl). Only elbow flexor supplied by the radial nerve.

name: Triceps brachii
origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle; lateral and medial heads: posterior humerus
insertion: Olecranon process of ulna
notes: Only the long head crosses the shoulder. Key for push-up transfers. Also covered in u3-s2 and u4-s7.

name: Anconeus
origin: Posterior lateral epicondyle of humerus
insertion: Lateral olecranon and posterior proximal ulna
notes: Small; assists triceps and stabilizes the elbow.

name: Supinator
origin: Lateral epicondyle, radial collateral and annular ligaments, supinator crest of ulna
insertion: Lateral surface of proximal 1/3 of radius
notes: Supinates in any elbow position; deep radial (posterior interosseous) nerve passes through it. Also in u3-s2.

name: Pronator teres
origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon) and coronoid process of ulna
insertion: Middle of lateral radius
notes: Median nerve passes between its two heads (pronator syndrome).

name: Pronator quadratus
origin: Distal 1/4 of anterior ulna
insertion: Distal 1/4 of anterior radius
notes: Prime pronator in any elbow position; anterior interosseous branch of median nerve.

name: Flexor carpi radialis
origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon)
insertion: Palmar base of 2nd (and 3rd) metacarpal
stretch: Wrist extension + ulnar deviation with elbow extended
notes: FCR.

name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon), olecranon and posterior ulnar border
insertion: Pisiform, hook of hamate, base of 5th metacarpal
stretch: Wrist extension + radial deviation with elbow extended
notes: FCU; ulnar nerve runs between its heads (cubital tunnel).

name: Palmaris longus
origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon)
insertion: Flexor retinaculum and palmar aponeurosis
notes: PL; absent in about 14% of people; common tendon graft donor.

name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
origin: Distal lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus
insertion: Dorsal base of 2nd metacarpal
stretch: Wrist flexion + ulnar deviation with elbow extended
notes: ECRL; key wrist extensor for tenodesis grasp (C6 SCI).

name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
origin: Lateral epicondyle (common extensor tendon)
insertion: Dorsal base of 3rd metacarpal
notes: ECRB; most often involved in lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow).

name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
origin: Lateral epicondyle (common extensor tendon) and posterior ulna
insertion: Dorsal base of 5th metacarpal
stretch: Wrist flexion + radial deviation with elbow extended
notes: ECU.

name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon), coronoid process, anterior radius
insertion: Sides of middle phalanges D2-5
stretch: Wrist and finger MCP/PIP extension with elbow extended
notes: FDS; prime PIP flexor. Tested by holding other fingers extended.

name: Flexor digitorum profundus
origin: Proximal anterior and medial ulna, interosseous membrane
insertion: Palmar bases of distal phalanges D2-5
notes: FDP; only DIP flexor. Median (anterior interosseous) to D2-3, ulnar to D4-5.

name: Flexor pollicis longus
origin: Anterior radius and interosseous membrane
insertion: Palmar base of distal phalanx of thumb
notes: FPL; only thumb IP flexor (tip pinch).

name: Abductor pollicis longus
origin: Posterior radius and ulna, interosseous membrane
insertion: Lateral base of 1st metacarpal
stretch: Thumb flexion/adduction with wrist ulnar deviation
notes: APL; lateral border of snuffbox. Inflamed with EPB in De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

name: Extensor pollicis brevis
origin: Posterior radius and interosseous membrane
insertion: Dorsal base of proximal phalanx of thumb
stretch: Thumb flexion with wrist ulnar deviation (Finkelstein position)
notes: EPB; lateral border of snuffbox; De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

name: Extensor pollicis longus
origin: Middle posterior ulna and interosseous membrane
insertion: Dorsal base of distal phalanx of thumb
notes: EPL; medial (ulnar) border of the anatomical snuffbox; hooks around Lister's tubercle.

name: Extensor digitorum
origin: Lateral epicondyle (common extensor tendon)
insertion: Extensor hood to middle and distal phalanges D2-5
stretch: Wrist flexion + finger flexion with elbow extended
notes: ED; prime MCP extensor; PIP/DIP extension aided by interossei and lumbricals.

name: Extensor indicis
origin: Posterior distal ulna and interosseous membrane
insertion: Extensor hood of index finger (D2)
notes: Lets the index finger point independently.

name: Extensor digiti minimi
origin: Lateral epicondyle (common extensor tendon)
insertion: Extensor hood of little finger (D5)

name: Abductor pollicis brevis
origin: Flexor retinaculum, scaphoid and trapezium tubercles
insertion: Radial base of proximal phalanx of thumb
notes: Thenar (OAF). Atrophies in carpal tunnel syndrome.

name: Flexor pollicis brevis
origin: Superficial head: flexor retinaculum, trapezium; deep head: trapezoid, capitate
insertion: Radial base of proximal phalanx of thumb
notes: Thenar (OAF). Superficial head median, deep head ulnar.

name: Opponens pollicis
origin: Flexor retinaculum and trapezium
insertion: Lateral (radial) border of 1st metacarpal
stretch: Thumb reposition (extension and abduction away from palm)
notes: Thenar (OAF). Loss gives 'ape hand'.

name: Abductor digiti minimi
origin: Pisiform and FCU tendon
insertion: Ulnar base of proximal phalanx of D5
notes: Hypothenar (OAF).

name: Flexor digiti minimi
origin: Hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum
insertion: Ulnar base of proximal phalanx of D5
notes: Hypothenar (OAF). Also called flexor digiti minimi brevis.

name: Opponens digiti minimi
origin: Hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum
insertion: Ulnar border of 5th metacarpal
notes: Hypothenar (OAF); cups the palm.

name: Adductor pollicis
origin: Oblique head: capitate, bases of 2nd-3rd metacarpals; transverse head: palmar 3rd metacarpal shaft
insertion: Ulnar base of proximal phalanx of thumb
notes: Deep palm (AIL); key pinch muscle. Weakness gives positive Froment's sign.

name: Dorsal interossei (4)
origin: Adjacent sides of all metacarpals (two heads)
insertion: Bases of proximal phalanges and extensor hoods of D2-4
stretch: Finger adduction; MCP extension with IP flexion
notes: DAB: dorsal ABduct away from the middle finger. Only intrinsics on the back of the hand.

name: Palmar interossei (3)
origin: Palmar surfaces of metacarpals 2, 4, 5
insertion: Proximal phalanges and extensor hoods of D2, 4, 5
stretch: Finger abduction; MCP extension with IP flexion
notes: PAD: palmar ADduct toward the middle finger.

name: Lumbricals (4)
origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus
insertion: Radial side of extensor hoods of D2-5
stretch: MCP extension with PIP/DIP flexion (claw position)
notes: Lumbricals 1-2 median, 3-4 ulnar. Produce the 'intrinsic plus' (tabletop) position; loss contributes to claw hand.

name: Psoas major
origin: Bodies, discs and transverse processes T12-L5
insertion: Lesser trochanter of femur
notes: With iliacus forms the iliopsoas, prime hip flexor. Tightness increases anterior pelvic tilt/lordosis.

name: Iliacus
origin: Iliac fossa
insertion: Lesser trochanter (with psoas tendon)
notes: Part of the iliopsoas.

name: Sartorius
origin: ASIS
insertion: Proximal medial tibia (pes anserine)
stretch: Hip extension, adduction, medial rotation with knee extension
notes: Longest muscle; 'tailor's muscle' (cross-legged sitting). Pes anserine member.

name: Pectineus
origin: Superior pubic ramus (pectineal line of pubis)
insertion: Pectineal line of femur

name: Adductor longus
origin: Body of pubis below pubic crest
insertion: Middle 1/3 of linea aspera
notes: Most commonly strained adductor (groin pull).

name: Adductor brevis
origin: Body and inferior ramus of pubis
insertion: Pectineal line and proximal linea aspera

name: Adductor magnus
origin: Inferior pubic ramus, ischial ramus, ischial tuberosity
insertion: Linea aspera, gluteal tuberosity and adductor tubercle
notes: Largest adductor; posterior 'hamstring' part is supplied by the tibial portion of the sciatic nerve.

name: Gracilis
origin: Body and inferior ramus of pubis
insertion: Proximal medial tibia (pes anserine)
notes: Only adductor that crosses the knee. Pes anserine member.

name: Gluteus maximus
origin: Posterior ilium, sacrum, coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament
insertion: Gluteal tuberosity of femur and IT band
stretch: Hip flexion, adduction, medial rotation (knee to opposite shoulder)
notes: Prime hip extender for sit-to-stand, stairs and running; weakness gives a backward trunk lurch in gait.

name: Piriformis
origin: Anterior sacrum
insertion: Superior greater trochanter
stretch: Hip medial rotation; with hip flexed, flexion + adduction (knee toward opposite shoulder)
notes: Deep 6 lateral rotator. Sciatic nerve usually exits below it (piriformis syndrome). Becomes a medial rotator/abductor when the hip is flexed past about 60 degrees.

name: Obturator internus
origin: Inner surface of obturator membrane and surrounding pelvis
insertion: Medial greater trochanter (trochanteric fossa region)
notes: Deep 6 lateral rotator.

name: Gemellus superior
origin: Ischial spine
insertion: Medial greater trochanter (with obturator internus tendon)
notes: Deep 6 lateral rotator.

name: Gemellus inferior
origin: Ischial tuberosity
insertion: Medial greater trochanter (with obturator internus tendon)
notes: Deep 6 lateral rotator.

name: Quadratus femoris
origin: Lateral ischial tuberosity
insertion: Quadrate tubercle on intertrochanteric crest
notes: Deep 6 lateral rotator.

name: Obturator externus
origin: Outer surface of obturator membrane and surrounding pubis/ischium
insertion: Trochanteric fossa of femur
notes: Deep 6 lateral rotator. Only deep rotator supplied by the obturator nerve.

name: Gluteus medius
origin: Outer ilium between anterior and posterior gluteal lines (below iliac crest)
insertion: Lateral greater trochanter
stretch: Hip adduction (leg crossed behind the other)
notes: Prime abductor. Weakness gives Trendelenburg sign/gait (opposite pelvis drops).

name: Gluteus minimus
origin: Outer ilium between anterior and inferior gluteal lines
insertion: Anterior greater trochanter
notes: Deep to gluteus medius; helps keep the pelvis level.

name: Tensor fasciae latae
origin: ASIS and anterior outer iliac crest
insertion: Lateral tibial condyle (Gerdy's tubercle) via IT band
stretch: Hip extension, adduction, lateral rotation (Ober position)
notes: Tight IT band contributes to lateral knee pain (IT band syndrome).

name: Rectus femoris
origin: AIIS (and just above acetabulum)
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via patella and patellar tendon
notes: Only quadriceps that crosses the hip (2-joint). Also covered in u6-s7.

name: Vastus lateralis
origin: Greater trochanter, intertrochanteric line, lateral lip of linea aspera
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via patella and patellar tendon
notes: Largest quadriceps; 1-joint.

name: Vastus medialis
origin: Intertrochanteric line and medial lip of linea aspera
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via patella and patellar tendon
notes: VMO fibers resist lateral patellar tracking; 1-joint.

name: Vastus intermedius
origin: Anterior and lateral shaft of femur (proximal 2/3)
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via patella and patellar tendon
notes: Deep to rectus femoris; 1-joint.

name: Semitendinosus
origin: Ischial tuberosity
insertion: Proximal medial tibia (pes anserine)
stretch: Hip flexion + knee extension (+ knee lateral rotation)
notes: Medial hamstring; pes anserine member. Also in u6-s9.

name: Semimembranosus
origin: Ischial tuberosity
insertion: Posterior medial tibial condyle
stretch: Hip flexion + knee extension (+ knee lateral rotation)
notes: Medial hamstring. Also in u6-s9.

name: Biceps femoris
origin: Long head: ischial tuberosity; short head: lateral lip of linea aspera
insertion: Head of fibula (and lateral tibial condyle)
stretch: Hip flexion + knee extension (+ knee medial rotation)
notes: Lateral hamstring. Long head 2-joint (tibial portion); short head 1-joint (common fibular portion). Also in u6-s9.

name: Popliteus
origin: Lateral femoral condyle (and lateral meniscus)
insertion: Posterior proximal tibia above soleal line
stretch: Knee extension with tibial lateral rotation
notes: 'Key that unlocks the knee' - reverses screw-home rotation to begin flexion.

name: Gastrocnemius
origin: Medial and lateral femoral condyles (posterior)
insertion: Calcaneal tuberosity via calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
notes: Triceps surae (with soleus); 2-joint. Active insufficiency with knee flexed. Also in u3-s2 and u6-s9.

name: Soleus
origin: Posterior head and proximal fibula, soleal line of tibia
insertion: Calcaneal tuberosity via calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
notes: Triceps surae; 1-joint postural muscle in standing. Seated heel raise isolates it. Also in u3-s2.

name: Plantaris
origin: Lateral supracondylar line of femur
insertion: Calcaneus (medial to or with the calcaneal tendon)
notes: Small and absent in some people; long thin tendon.

name: Tibialis anterior
origin: Lateral tibial condyle, proximal 2/3 lateral tibia, interosseous membrane
insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of 1st metatarsal
notes: Prime dorsiflexor; weakness (fibular nerve injury) causes foot drop/steppage gait. Lowers the foot eccentrically after heel strike.

name: Extensor hallucis longus
origin: Middle anterior fibula and interosseous membrane
insertion: Dorsal base of distal phalanx of great toe
notes: EHL; L5 myotome test.

name: Extensor digitorum longus
origin: Lateral tibial condyle, proximal 3/4 anterior fibula, interosseous membrane
insertion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2-5 (dorsal expansion)
notes: EDL.

name: Fibularis tertius
origin: Distal 1/3 anterior fibula and interosseous membrane
insertion: Dorsal base of 5th metatarsal
notes: Peroneus tertius; often blends with EDL; absent in some people.

name: Fibularis longus
origin: Head and proximal 2/3 lateral fibula
insertion: Plantar medial cuneiform and base of 1st metatarsal
notes: Peroneus longus; tendon passes behind lateral malleolus and under the foot to support the transverse and lateral arches ('stirrup' with tibialis anterior).

name: Fibularis brevis
origin: Distal 2/3 lateral fibula
insertion: Tuberosity of base of 5th metatarsal
notes: Peroneus brevis; inversion sprains can avulse its insertion (5th metatarsal base fracture).

name: Tibialis posterior
origin: Posterior tibia, fibula and interosseous membrane
insertion: Navicular tuberosity, cuneiforms, cuboid, bases of metatarsals 2-4
notes: Main dynamic support of the medial arch; dysfunction leads to adult-acquired flatfoot. 'Tom' in Tom, Dick and Harry.

name: Flexor hallucis longus
origin: Distal 2/3 posterior fibula and interosseous membrane
insertion: Plantar base of distal phalanx of great toe
notes: FHL; push-off in gait. 'Harry' behind the medial malleolus.

name: Flexor digitorum longus
origin: Middle posterior tibia (below soleal line)
insertion: Plantar bases of distal phalanges of toes 2-5
notes: FDL. 'Dick' behind the medial malleolus.
